name: bind
synopsis: int bind(int sockfd, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addrlen);
description: bind() assigns the address specified by addr to the socket referred to by the file descriptor sockfd. It is normally necessary to assign a local address using bind() before a SOCK_STREAM socket can receive connections. The rules for name binding vary by address family.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the socket to bind.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Pointer to the address structure to assign to the socket.

parameters.name: addrlen
parameters.description: Size, in bytes, of the address structure pointed to by addr.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The address is protected, and the user is not the superuser.
The given address is already in use.
sockfd is not a valid file descriptor.
The socket is already bound, or addrlen is wrong, or addr is not valid for this socket's domain.
The file descriptor sockfd does not refer to a socket.
A nonexistent interface was requested or the requested address was not local.
addr points outside the user's accessible address space.
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving addr.
A component in the directory prefix of the socket pathname does not exist.
A component of the path prefix is not a directory.
The socket inode would reside on a read-only filesystem.

bugs: The transparent proxy options are not described.
